kangaroo-at-2009-student-04.prompt: Mari, Ville and Ossi are going to a coffee shop. Each of them has 3 glasses of juice, 2 cups of ice cream and 5 biscuits. What value could the total bill come to in the end?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-06.prompt: The circles $k_1$ (with centre $M_1$ and radius 13) and $k_2$ (with centre $M_2$ and radius 15) intersect each other in the points $P$ and $Q$. The length of the segment $PQ$ is 24. What could the distance $M_1M_2$ be?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-07.prompt: In a drawer there are 2 white, 3 red and 4 blue socks. Lisa knows that one third of the socks have holes but she does not know the colour of the faulty socks. She randomly picks socks from the drawer until she has a pair that is usable, i.e. she has a pair without holes and of equal colour. What is the minimum number of socks she has to draw to be certain to get a usable pair?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-08.prompt: The square in the diagram has side length 1. What is the radius of the small circle?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-09.prompt: Each side of a triangle $ABC$ is extended to the points $P, Q, R, S, T$ and $U$, so that $PA = AB = BS$, $TC = CA = AQ$ and $UC = CB = BR$. The area of $ABC$ is 1. What is the area of the hexagon $PQRSTU$?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-10.prompt: In the diagram on the right we want to colour the fields with the colours A, B, C and D so that adjacent fields are always in different colours. (Even fields that share only one corner count as adjacent.) Some fields have already been coloured in. In which colour can the grey field be coloured?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-11.prompt: A (very small) ball is kicked off from point $A$ on a square billiard table with side length 2 m. After moving along the shown path and touching the sides three times as indicated, the path ends in point $B$. How long is the path that the ball travels from $A$ to $B$? (As indicated on the right: angle of incidence = angle of reflection.)

kangaroo-at-2009-student-12.prompt: In a group of 2009 kangaroos each one is either light or dark. The smallest of the light kangaroos is bigger than exactly 8 dark kangaroos. One light one is bigger than exactly 9 dark ones, another light one is bigger than exactly 10 dark ones, and so on. Exactly one light kangaroo is bigger than all dark kangaroos. How many light kangaroos are there?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-13.prompt: In the diagram to the right a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cube is made up of four transparent $1 \times 1 \times 1$ cubes and four non-transparent black $1 \times 1 \times 1$ cubes. They are placed in such a way that the entire big cube is non-transparent; i.e. looking at it from the front to the back, from the right to the left, or from the top to the bottom, at no point can you look through the cube. What is the minimum number of black $1 \times 1 \times 1$ cubes needed to make a $3 \times 3 \times 3$ cube non-transparent in the same way?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-15.prompt: Determine the units digit of the number $1^2 - 2^2 + 3^2 - \dots - 2008^2 + 2009^2$.

kangaroo-at-2009-student-18.prompt: 100 students take an exam with 4 questions. 90 solve the first question, 85 the second, 80 the third and 70 the fourth. Determine the smallest possible number of students that have solved all four questions.

kangaroo-at-2009-student-19.prompt: In the diagram on the right we see the bird's-eye view and front elevation of a solid that is bounded by flat surfaces (i.e. the view from above and from the front respectively). Which of the outlines I to IV can be the side elevation (i.e. view from the left) of the same object?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-20.prompt: The sum of the numbers in each row, column and diagonal of the "magic square" on the right is always the same. Only two numbers are visible. Which number is missing in field $a$?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-21.prompt: Two runners each run laps around a racetrack at constant speed. Both start at the same time at the same point. $A$ is faster than $B$, takes 3 minutes to cover one lap and overtakes $B$ for the first time after 8 minutes. How long does $B$ take to cover one lap?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-22.prompt: Let $Z$ be the number of 8-digit numbers whose digits are all different and not equal to 0. How many of those numbers are divisible by 9?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-24.prompt: For how many whole numbers $n \ge 3$ does a convex polygon exist whose angles are in the ratio $1 : 2 : \dots : n$?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-25.prompt: 55 pupils are taking part in a competition. A jury marks each question with a "+" if it is solved correctly, with a "−" if it is solved incorrectly and with a "0" if it was not attempted. It turns out that no two students had both the same number of "+" and the same number of "−". What is the minimum number of questions that had to be asked in the competition?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-26.prompt: In a rectangle $JKLM$ the angle bisector at $J$ intersects the diagonal $KM$ in $N$. The distance of $N$ to $LM$ is 1 and the distance of $N$ to $KL$ is 8. How long is $LM$?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-27.prompt: If $k = \dfrac{a}{b+c} = \dfrac{b}{c+a} = \dfrac{c}{a+b}$, how many possible real values exist for $k$?

kangaroo-at-2009-student-28.prompt:
The numbers $1, 2, 3, \dots, 99$ are divided into $n$ groups. The following rules apply:

- Each number is in exactly one group.
- There are at least two numbers in each group.
- If two numbers are in the same group, then their sum is not divisible by 3.

Determine the smallest $n$ which fulfils these rules.

kangaroo-at-2009-student-29.prompt: Samantha and her three sisters go to the theatre. They have reserved a box with four seats. Samantha and two of her sisters arrive early and sit down without paying attention to their seat numbers. Marie arrives later and insists on sitting on the seat that is indicated on her ticket. What is the probability that Samantha has to change her seat, if now every sister who has to change seats insists on sitting on the seat indicated on her ticket?
